observations.body: David fasts and lies on the ground while the child lives; after death he washes, worships, eats, answers his servants, comforts Bathsheba, and a son named Solomon is born and loved.

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 12:16–25 as its own taking, rebuke, and house fracture David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places grief changes its bodily form after the child’s death while another son is born inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
